subject: technology
topic: People cannot tell AI faces from real ones, and trust the fake ones more
angle: While AI-synthesized faces are indistinguishable from and more trustworthy than real faces, human detection accuracy is currently at chance levels but can be improved through specific interventions.
title: The Trust in Synthetic Faces

hooks.text: Can you tell who is real?
You think you can spot fakes. You cannot.
You are trusting faces that do not exist.
A screen glows in a dark room.

reveal.headline: AI faces are rated as more trustworthy than real faces.
reveal.body: Studies show that synthetic faces are indistinguishable from human ones and earn higher trust ratings. You are more likely to believe a person who does not exist.

explain.headline: Your brain is currently unable to detect these fakes.
explain.body: Human accuracy in detecting deepfakes is currently at chance levels. While certain interventions can improve this, your natural ability to spot synthetic faces is limited.

matters.headline: Your sense of trust is being bypassed.
matters.body: That may be why you feel a connection to digital personas. If a fake face is more trustworthy than a real one, your intuition is no longer a reliable filter.

example.headline: A profile picture on a social feed.
example.body: You scroll past a face in a comment thread. You feel a sense of sincerity from their expression. That person is a calculation of pixels, not a human life.

stat.label: human accuracy in detecting deepfake images

claims.text: AI-synthesized faces are indistinguishable from real faces and are rated as more trustworthy than real faces.
claims.quote: Our evaluation of the photorealism of AI-synthesized faces indicates that synthesis engines have passed through the uncanny valley and are capable of creating faces that are indistinguishable-and more trustworthy-than real faces.

claims.text: People's accuracy in detecting deepfakes is 53.16% [42.12, 64.64], k = 18 for images, which is below the chance level of 35%.
claims.quote: for images, 53. 16% [42. 12, 64. 64], k = 18; for text, 52. 00% [37. 42, 65. 88], k = 15; and for video, 57. 31% [47. 80, 66. 57], k = 26. Odds ratios were 0. 64 [0. 52, 0. 79], k = 62, indicating 39% detection accuracy, below chance (audio 45%, image 35%, text 40%, video 40%).

claims.text: Synthesized human deepfake detection is at chance for different modalities.
claims.quote: Synthesized human deepfake detection is at chance for different modalities.

claims.text: Manipulations designed to disrupt visual processing of faces hinder human participants' performance while mostly not affecting the model's performance.
claims.quote: We find that manipulations designed to disrupt visual processing of faces hinder human participants' performance while mostly not affecting the model's performance, suggesting a role for specialized cognitive capacities in explaining human deepfake detection performance.

claims.text: Detection accuracy varies widely, with some studies showing humans outperforming AI models and others indicating the opposite.
claims.quote: Detection accuracy varies widely, with some studies showing humans outperforming AI models and others indicating the opposite.

claims.text: Strategies like feedback training, AI support, and deepfake caricaturization improved detection performance above chance levels (65.14% [55.21, 74.46], k = 15), especially for video stimuli.
claims.quote: Moreover, d' values show no significant difference from chance. However, strategies like feedback training, AI support, and deepfake caricaturization improved detection performance above chance levels (65. 14% [55. 21, 74. 46], k = 15), especially for video stimuli.

verdict: The evidence confirms that AI faces can be more trustworthy than real ones and that humans currently struggle to detect them at rates better than chance.
caveat: Detection performance is influenced by a complex interplay of factors including person-level cognitive abilities and stimuli-level factors like deepfake quality.
caption: AI-synthesized faces are now indistinguishable from real ones and are rated as more trustworthy. Research shows that humans currently struggle to detect these deepfakes at rates better than chance. Detection performance is influenced by a complex interplay of factors including person-level cognitive abilities and stimuli-level factors like deepfake quality. Who are you trusting today?
